assertions.description: The mobile app sends every request through the gateway.
The web app sends every request through the gateway.
Clients upload the original straight to object storage with a signed URL, bypassing the gateway.
The gateway checks the caller's access token with the auth service.
The gateway routes photo posts to the upload service.
The gateway routes feed requests to the feed service.
The upload service records the new photo as processing.
The upload service publishes PhotoUploaded to the queue (never the reverse).
Workers consume PhotoUploaded from the queue (consumer → topic, as RELATION_TYPES defines subscribes).
Workers read the original and write the thumbnails back.
Workers mark the photo ready.
Workers publish PhotoReady.
The feed service consumes PhotoReady.
The feed service reads photo metadata.
The feed service keeps ready-made feed pages in the cache.
The feed service asks the push provider to alert followers.
The CDN reads photos and thumbnails from object storage.
The decoupling decision justifies the queue.
The signed-URL decision justifies the upload service's narrow role and the direct upload.
Keeping metadata apart justifies a separate metadata database.
The disposable-cache decision explains the cache's role.
The buy-not-build decision justifies the external CDN (and push provider).
The queue never points back at the upload service.
